title: 1976 AHSME Problem 20
statement: Let \(a,\) \(b\) and \(x\) be positive real numbers distinct from one. Then \[ \begin{aligned} 4(\log_a x)^2&+3(\log_b x)^2\\ &=8(\log_a x)(\log_b x) \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
Factoring gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\bigl(2\log_a x-\log_b x\bigr)\\ &\quad\cdot \bigl(2\log_a x-3\log_b x\bigr)=0. \end{aligned} \] Since \(x\ne1,\) change of base shows that the first factor vanishes when \(a=b^2,\) while the second vanishes when \(a^3=b^2.\) Thus the equation holds under either of two conditions, and no listed “if and only if” statement describes their union.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Move all terms to one side and factor the quadratic in the two logarithms
Translate each factor equation into a relation between the bases using change of base
